01 · The Engineer & Philosophy

Building sovereign software for people who work in the real world.

I am an independent Android developer and the founder of VaidikTech. My journey began with deep curiosity about how software interacts with hardware and how it can eliminate friction in overlooked everyday businesses.

Over time, curiosity matured into an uncompromising engineering ethos: never build superficial demos or theoretical coursework prototypes. I build complete, hardened applications that real pawnbrokers, advocates, jewellers, and solo tradespeople depend upon every single day.

Operating in India means designing for hostile constraints: sporadic 2G/3G connectivity, dense basements with zero cellular reception, blinding outdoor sunlight, and zero tolerance for fractional currency drift. That is why my apps strictly mandate Zero INTERNET Permissions, 256-bit SQLCipher AES, and integer paise monetary mathematics.

I am currently pursuing my B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering, specialising in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning at Lakshmi Narain College of Technology (LNCT), Bhopal.

04 · The Engineering Process

How I Build: From Raw Problem to Production Release

A disciplined engineering lifecycle engineered to deliver offline sovereignty, zero financial rounding drift, and instant hardware response times.

01

Problem & Field Workflow Discovery

Observe how pawnbrokers, advocates, and jewellers actually operate. Identify non-negotiable constraints: zero cellular reception in basements, bright sunlight, and physical receipts.

02

Sovereign Architecture Design

Mandate zero remote cloud dependencies. Architect Room SQLite with SQLCipher 256-bit AES encryption sealed inside hardware Android Keystore MasterKey.

03

Zero-Drift Financial Engineering

Forbid Float and Double in monetary math. Every rupee is strictly stored as Long (paise) with standard Indian numbering grouping (₹1,23,456).

04

Native Android & Hardware Integration

Build single-Activity Jetpack Compose Material 3 UIs, CameraX photo evidence pipelines, Bluetooth ESC/POS 58mm/80mm thermal printing, and Google Nearby P2P clusters.

05

Play Store Release & Hardening

R8 ProGuard resource shrinking, OWASP MASVS mobile security audits, signed production bundles (JKS), and automated Google Play Console lifecycle releases.

06

Field Reliability & Iteration

Dual-mode AES-256-GCM backups with PBKDF2 (600,000 iterations), automated daily WorkManager tasks, and continuous statutory law amendment updates.

System Architecture Explorer

Core Engineering Patterns in Production

AdvoKosh: Sovereign Chamber Privacy Pattern

All client dossiers, court orders, and voice dictations are stored in a sandboxed Room database encrypted with SQLCipher 256-bit AES-CBC.

The encryption passphrase is never stored in SharedPreferences. Instead, it is generated at first boot and sealed inside the device?Ts hardware Secure Enclave via MasterKey (AES-256-GCM).

✓ Zero Telemetry✓ Zero Firebase Sockets✓ DPDP Act 2023 Compliant

05 · Real Implementation Code

Production Kotlin & Compose Codebase

Real excerpts from live commercial applications showing hardware keystore cryptographic sealing, integer paise value classes, and GPU vision pipelines.

Android Studio Ladybug · Kotlin 2.0.21
// Hardware-Backed Sovereign Chamber Database Factory
@Singleton
class ChamberDatabaseFactory @Inject constructor(
    @ApplicationContext private val context: Context
) {
    fun createEncryptedDatabase(): VakalatDatabase {
        // 1. Generate or retrieve hardware-backed MasterKey (AES-256-GCM)
        val masterKey = MasterKey.Builder(context)
            .setKeyScheme(MasterKey.KeyScheme.AES256_GCM)
            .setRequestStrongBoxBacked(true) // Hardware SE Enclave
            .build()

        // 2. Retrieve secure database passphrase
        val passphrase = getOrCreateChamberPassphrase(context, masterKey)
        val openHelperFactory = SupportFactory(SQLiteDatabase.getBytes(passphrase))

        // 3. Build encrypted Room database with SQLCipher
        return Room.databaseBuilder(context, VakalatDatabase::class.java, "advokosh.db")
            .openHelperFactory(openHelperFactory)
            .addMigrations(MIGRATION_1_2, MIGRATION_2_3, MIGRATION_3_4)
            .fallbackToDestructiveMigrationOnDowngrade()
            .build()
    }
}
